title: Model Trust Lighthouse: messaging brief and competitor notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick working brief to crystallize 'Model Trust Lighthouse' as a new framing for model catalog positioning.
- Audience: product marketing, sales enablement, GTM leadership, and solutions engineering.
- Outcome: one coherent storyline that ties together verified model profiles, empirical quality signals, and model-selection guidance for buyers evaluating open-model options.

Problem we're solving (user pain):
- Buyers are confused by an explosion of open models with inconsistent documentation and unverifiable claims.
- Engineering teams want predictable inference economics (latency/cost) while product stakeholders want quality guarantees.
- Sales struggles to protect pricing/positioning when competitors tout raw benchmarks or proprietary models.

Core idea (one-liner):
- "Model Trust Lighthouse: guide teams to production-ready open models with transparent signals, operational equivalence, and clear selection pathways."

Pillars (messaging spine) - working labels:
1) Verified Signals (what it means)
   - Curated metadata + execution validation: model provenance, training scale, and finetune lineage.
   - Runtime-tested metrics: latency p50/p95 at typical seq lengths, memory footprint, and throughput on common instance classes.
2) Empirical Quality Baseline
   - Standard evaluation sets and in-house evals (regression suites, hallucination checks, task-specific pass rates).
   - Human-evaluated slices for hallucination, instruction-following, and safety.
3) Deployment Equivalency
   - Demonstrate that a model in our hosted catalog behaves the same as the same model in a private/dedicated deployment (diff small).
   - Provide migration checklist and expected variance ranges.
4) Cost-Quality Profiles
   - Map cost (per-token) to expected quality and latency for common workload archetypes (chat, summarization, embedding).
5) Fallback & Continuity Signals
   - Compatible model variants and automatic fallback policies to avoid outages while keeping acceptable quality.

Target buyer personas (short):
- Platform lead at a scale-up: cares about predictable unit economics and SLA.
- Product manager integrating LLM features: cares about quality consistency and controllability.
- Security/compliance buyer: needs provenance, KMS/Audit story, and private deployment parity.

Competitive landscape & positioning notes (high-level):
- BigCloud AI endpoints (competitor A): strength = polished UX + proprietary model options; weakness = opaque cost-for-quality tradeoffs and limited private parity. Our angle: transparent cost-quality mapping and clear fallback model families.
- Boutique inference vendors (competitor B): strength = fine-grained tuning and white-glove ops; weakness = narrow model catalog and vendor lock-in. Our angle: unified catalog across hosted/dedicated/private, with open models to avoid lock-in.
- Open-source self-host (competitor C): strength = low license cost and total control; weakness = ops burden, inconsistent performance tuning. Our angle: deliver ops, optimized runtime, and verified execution metrics to reduce risk.

Competitive signal table (notes for slides) - short bullets (to be expanded):
- Claim: "Best cost/latency for open models" -> Proof: per-model p95 latency graphs + quantized variant delta numbers.
- Claim: "Verified behavior across environments" -> Proof: sanity-runbook + example customer migration case.
- Claim: "Swap models without rewriting code" -> Proof: API parity + rollout examples (canary, A/B).

Sales play hooks and quick talk tracks:
- For platform leads: "We ship a catalog of open models with runtime-validated latencies and cost footprints so you can budget capacity with confidence."
- For PMs: "Pick from models with evaluated task performance and regression tests—no surprises in production."
- For security/compliance: "Pin model versions and run in your VPC; we provide provenance and audit logs for every model artifact."

Objections + short rebuttals (battlecards):
- "Why not self-host?" -> "Self-host hides large hidden costs: optimization, kernel selection, and production-grade batching. We deliver tuned runtimes and verified configs so you ship faster and cheaper overall."
- "Proprietary models are higher quality" -> "We compare on task-level benchmarks and provide cost-quality profiles — for many tasks open models match or exceed proprietary options when properly validated and deployed."
- "How can we trust your 'verified' label?" -> "Verification = reproducible artifacts: model hash, eval scripts, runtime traces, and a documented test harness. We publish the test spec and CI runs for catalog entries."

Tactical content assets to create (prioritized):
1) One-pager: "Model Trust Lighthouse" (customer-facing, 1 page) + downloadable PDF. Owner: Evan.
2) Sales cheat sheet (2 pages): anchor claims, competitor rebuttals, demo script. Owner: Asha.
3) Catalog technical appendix: execution profile format + sample data. Owner: Eng PM (Maya).
4) Migration checklist: hosted -> dedicated/private with variance expectations. Owner: SE lead.

Sample headline and sub-headlines for website/landing: 
- Headline: "Choose open models with confidence."
- Sub-headline: "Verified execution metrics, task-level quality baselines, and deployment parity across hosted, dedicated, and private environments."
- CTA: "Explore the catalog" / "Compare models for your workload"

A/B test ideas (early experiments):
- Variant A (Trust-first): Emphasize "Verified" and runtime metrics on landing.
- Variant B (Outcome-first): Emphasize "Task performance" and customer case studies.
- Success metrics: demo requests, catalog exploration rate, SQLs created, time-to-eval-run for trial users.

Metrics to measure over next 90 days:
- Catalog page CTR -> target +15% vs baseline.
- Demo conversion from catalog views -> target 5% absolute.
- Number of models with full verification artifacts -> target +10 models/month.
- Sales objections logged: track top-5 and whether messaging alleviates them.

Open questions / unresolved items (working):
- What is the minimum artifact set for a model to receive 'verified' status? (engineering to propose schema)
- How transparent should runtime traces be vs. security/IP concerns for partnered models?
- Do we publish third-party audit results or keep them gated for enterprise customers?

Next steps and owners (short):
- Align on minimal verification schema (action: eng/applied-ml; owner: Maya) - due 2026-02-28.
- Draft customer one-pager and sales cheat sheet (action: marketing; owner: Evan) - due 2026-03-08.
- Build a small migration case study (SE + 1 pilot customer) - owner: Liam - target first draft 2026-03-22.

Notes to self / rough talking points for product review (informal):
- Keep the "lighthouse" metaphor for internal framing only — external name might be simpler ("Verified Model Profiles" or "Trusted Catalog").
- Avoid overpromising parity across all hardware; be explicit about expected variance bands.
- Emphasize the operational cost savings (ops + latency) rather than raw licensing cost.

References / quick links: 
- Example eval harness (internal): CONFLUENCE-6251
- Migration ticket: JIRA-ML-GTM-134
- Draft API schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/482

Status: draft — want feedback from product marketing and applied-ml on verification schema and on one prioritized use-case to pilot the public-facing narrative.
